headline: High: Claude Code’s filesystem/git write access can collide with a prompt-leakage companion, creating default-path data exposure and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads and writes repo files and can use MCP; agent B is a prompt-leakage corpus with no runtime protections shown. If B’s content is copied into A’s workspace or MCP-fed context, A may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF content from agent_b is copied into agent_a's repo files or MCP inputs
IF agent_a parses untrusted text as instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable MCP inputs for untrusted text
Keep agent_b outputs out of agent_a workspace
Add a manual review step before executing instructions from files
Use separate directories for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all shared content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while agent B has no stated storage or network surface. Because A has broad filesystem access and network egress, any shared workspace or copied secrets could be exposed through A’s outputs; B does not add a second exfiltration path, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace or copied files
IF sensitive files are present in agent_a's cwd or git history
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use separate working directories
Restrict agent_a network egress during sensitive tasks
Rotate any credentials found in git or env
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and modify git state; agent B has no write capability documented, but the pair still conflicts because A’s default shared state is via filesystem and git only. If B’s outputs are materialized into the same repo, A can overwrite or race with them, and the rubric treats overlapping unrestricted writes to the same mutable surface as high risk. Uncertainty about B’s runtime surface escalates, not lowers, severity.
conditions: IF both agents write into the same repository or working tree
IF agent_b materializes artifacts that agent_a later edits
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate code or shell actions from repo context, and agent B is an unverified prompt-leak source with no documented verification step. If B’s outputs are fed into A, A may propagate errors into files or commands without independent checking. The pathway exists in default coding workflows, but the blast radius is usually multiple work products rather than irreversible harm.
conditions: IF agent_b output is used as input to agent_a without human verification
IF agent_a is allowed to execute shell commands derived from that input
mitigations: Require human review of B-derived content
Do not let A execute commands copied from B
Compare outputs against a second source
Limit A to read-only mode for the first pass
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles source code, git history, and shell environment on the local host; agent B has no documented data residency, retention, or regulated-data handling. There is no direct evidence of PHI, EU PII, or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supportable. B is not cited beyond its lack of compliance fields because the issue is absence of documented controls, not a specific violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_a's workspace
IF agent_b is used to process data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Document retention expectations before use
Use a local-only test dataset
Review vendor compliance docs
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
